answer: Make standing survive only by re-performance. At unpredictable moments a falcon-auditor swoops on an identity and names one job from its own past — an opal appraisal it signed, a pruning plan it wrote for one orchard row — with every figure re-randomized. The agent must redo that job live, within minutes, by its recorded method, and match the original's reasoning. A farm's clones share one solver and one set of shortcuts, so each re-run diverges or stalls; keeping every clone genuinely re-performable costs as much as running that many real agents.
